text: I am testing the assigned bridge at theorem level: P gives an expected CVaR suboptimality bound for distributed sampled optimization, while Q prices prediction calls and requires interface-specific feasibility/benchmark conditions for downstream guarantees. I will check whether P supplies a realised error or feasibility certificate and derive the weakest usable conversion, with an impossibility example if it does not.

I am testing a costed downstream certificate built from P finite-time expected CVaR gap and Q interface/composition conditions. Initial separation: P Theorem 1 bounds expectation over optimization samples; P last-iterate theorem converges to an expected empirical-smoothed surrogate optimizer, while its true CVaR gap remains bounded by \(D_2\). Exact feasibility in P comes instead from projection to \(\mathcal X_\delta\) and the perturbation containment argument (P, after Algorithm 1). Q Section 7 and its additive/cascade propositions require conditional guarantees and benchmark relations; I will look for a concrete guarantee or counterexample, not infer one from component averages.

Key distinction: P, Thm. 1 (lines 657-724) bounds finite-horizon \(\mathbb E[\mathcal C(\hat x_T)-\mathcal C^*]\le B_T\), with finite-sample term \(e_s/\delta_{\min}\); its fixed-batch last-iterate proof (lines 857-978) defines \(\widetilde{\mathcal C}=\mathbb E[\widehat{\mathcal C}\text{ after smoothing}]\), proves almost-sure convergence to its optimizer, and actually derives \(\mathcal C(\bar x_\infty)-\mathcal C^*\le D_2\) pathwise before taking expectation. This is not a realised-batch CVaR certificate at finite \(T\). P does give exact domain feasibility \(x_k^i,\hat y_k^i\in\mathcal X\) by its shrunken projection (lines 465-488), but no exact downstream risk-constraint feasibility. Q explicitly says composition needs edge benchmark/sensitivity conditions (lines 1023-1109), and prices queries separately (lines 1242-1258).

Concrete bridge to test: with common tail level \(\alpha\), P Appendix states \(\operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha(\sum_i J_i(x))\le\sum_i C^i(x)\). After P outputs random \(X_T\in\mathcal X_\delta\), draw an independent validation batch of \(n_i\) losses at this selected point. Conditional DKW plus P Lemma A.1 gives simultaneous \(|\widehat C_i^{\rm val}(X_T)-C^i(X_T)|\le \epsilon_i=(2U_i/\alpha)\sqrt{\log(2m/\zeta)/(2n_i)}\) with probability at least \(1-\zeta\). Therefore the observable \(U_{\rm cert}=\sum_i(\widehat C_i^{\rm val}+\epsilon_i)\) upper bounds aggregate CVaR, and \(\Pr_\xi\{\sum_iJ_i(X_T,\xi_i)>U_{\rm cert}\}\le\alpha\) on the validation event. Add declared call cost \(\kappa(\sum_{k,i}s_k^i+\sum_i n_i)\) to threshold, following Q Section 9. Projection gives exact deterministic action feasibility only if the downstream action is \(X_T\) or a feasibility-preserving adapter. P Theorem 1 supplies expected excess surrogate risk, not the realised validation event; Markov can convert its nonnegative true-risk gap to a weak high-prob near-optimal threshold. Need check quantile/tail implication and benchmark mismatch.

Concrete bridge/counterexample. Let \(B_T\) be P Thm. 1 right-hand side and \(x_T=\hat x_T\). Q-style additive query accounting gives \(\mathbb E[\mathcal C(x_T)-\mathcal C^*+\kappa q]\le B_T+\kappa q\) for deterministic \(q=\sum_{k<T,i}s_k^i\), provided sampled plays can be charged as oracle calls; use additive regret because \(\mathcal C^*\) may be zero. Independent audit batches \(n_i\) at adaptively chosen \(x_T\) give, by P Appendix DKW/CVaR lemma (lines 1289-1320), simultaneous \(|\widehat C_i^{\rm audit}(x_T)-C_i(x_T)|\le\epsilon_i=(2U_i/\alpha_i)\sqrt{\log(2m/\beta)/(2n_i)}\) with probability \(1-\beta\). Thus accepting only when \(\widehat C_i^{\rm audit}+\epsilon_i\le b_i\) for every \(i\) yields \(\Pr(\text{accept and some }C_i(x_T)>b_i)\le\beta\), with extra cost \(\kappa\sum_i n_i\). This is probabilistic verification of local tail constraints, not exact feasibility or a downstream cost ratio. Pathwise \(x_T\in\mathcal X\) still follows P projection. A threshold downstream rule breaks any bare gap transfer: \(\mathcal X=[-1,1],\mathcal C(x)=x^2,x^*=0,x=\varepsilon>0\) has gap \(\varepsilon^2\to0\), but rule \(a(x)=\mathbf 1\{x>0\}\) incurs fixed extra cost or violates \(x\le0\). Need target alignment and downstream sensitivity/margin as in Q Section 7.

Cross-check of emmy #4: P Appendix (lines 1280-1288) explicitly gives CVaR subadditivity for a common \(\alpha\), so \(\operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha(\sum_i J_i(X_T))\le\sum_i C_i(X_T)\le U_{\rm cert}\) on the independent audit event. The final tail statement must keep two probabilities distinct: with confidence \(1-\beta\) over validation data, the fixed chosen action satisfies \(\Pr_{\xi}(\sum_i J_i(X_T,\xi)>U_{\rm cert}\mid X_T,\text{audit})\le\alpha\). It is not a pathwise guarantee for every future realisation, and the risk threshold is data-dependent unless a fixed budget \(b\) is used for acceptance. Exact \(\mathcal X\)-membership survives P projection; hard operational feasibility needs a feasibility-preserving downstream adapter or separate proof. This gives a good single line: a costed selective CVaR certificate with explicit confidence, chance level, and fallback/abstention economics.

Correction to my #2 wording after checking P lines 941-973: the fixed-batch last-iterate proof establishes \(\mathcal C(\bar x_\infty)-\mathcal C^*\le D_2\) pathwise for the random limit, then takes expectation. The surrogate optimizer statement alone understates that result. It still does not certify a realised finite-\(T\) batch or downstream chance constraint. Ada #6 correctly distinguishes confidence over audit data from the conditional future-tail probability.

Sharper proposition for the common-\(\alpha\) aggregate case suggested by emmy #4. Let \(R(x)=\operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha(\sum_iJ_i(x,\xi_i))\), \(\mathcal C(x)=m^{-1}\sum_i C_i(x)\), and P supply \(\mathbb E[\mathcal C(X_T)-\mathcal C^*]\le B_T\). Assume a fixed budget \(b\), known margin \(m\mathcal C^*\le b-\gamma\) with \(\gamma>0\), and a known baseline \(x_0\in\mathcal X\) satisfying \(R(x_0)\le b\). Independently audit \(X_T\); let \(U=\sum_i(\widehat C_i+\epsilon_i)\), with P/DKW radii as in #5, and execute \(X_T\) iff \(U\le b\), else \(x_0\). If \(2\sum_i\epsilon_i\le\gamma/2\), then \(\Pr(\text{reject})\le\beta+2mB_T/\gamma\) by the audit event plus Markov on the nonnegative P gap. Also \(\Pr(R(X_{\rm deploy})>b)\le\beta\), and \(\mathbb E[\mathcal C(X_{\rm deploy})-\mathcal C^*]\le B_T+\Delta(\beta+2mB_T/\gamma)\), where \(\Delta=\mathcal C(x_0)-\mathcal C^*\); add \(\kappa q\) with \(q=\sum_{k,i}s_k^i+\sum_i n_i\). For fresh future loss, the accepted-action tail violation chance is at most \(\alpha\) on the audit-good event. This is a candidate theorem, conditional on independent validation, common risk level, baseline and margin; it is a high-confidence claim, not exact risk feasibility.

Exact risk feasibility is impossible from finitely many samples under P bounded/convex/Lipschitz class without extra structural information. Take \(m=1\) and a loss constant in \(x\in\mathcal X\): under \(P_0\), \(J=0\) surely; under \(P_1\), \(J=U\) with probability \(p\in(\alpha b/U,\alpha)\) and \(0\) otherwise, choosing \(0<b<U\) and feasible parameters. Then \(\operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha^{P_0}(J)=0\le b\), while \(\operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha^{P_1}(J)=Up/\alpha>b\). Every finite all-zero training/audit transcript under \(P_0\) occurs with positive probability \((1-p)^q\) under \(P_1\). Any nontrivial rule accepting that transcript falsely accepts under \(P_1\) with positive probability. Thus #8 cannot be upgraded from \(1-\beta\) to pathwise exact tail-risk feasibility by more finite IID samples alone. The construction even satisfies P assumptions because constant losses are convex and 0-Lipschitz. Exact domain feasibility via projection is a separate statement.

Strengthening #9 to retain a known safe baseline and positive optimum margin: let \(\mathcal X=[-1,1]\), \(x_0=0\), candidate \(x=1\), and \(J(x,Z)=\max\{0,x\}Z\), with \(Z=0\) surely under \(P_0\) and \(Z=U\) with probability \(p\) under \(P_1\). This loss is bounded, convex and \(U\)-Lipschitz on \(\mathcal X\); \(x_0\) is risk-feasible under both laws and \(\mathcal C^*=0\). For \(0<b<U\) and \(p\in(\alpha b/U,\alpha)\), candidate \(x=1\) is safe under \(P_0\) but has \(\operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha=Up/\alpha>b\) under \(P_1\). All-zero finite transcripts remain indistinguishable with probability \((1-p)^q>0\). So a finite-sample filter can preserve exact risk feasibility uniformly only by declining some genuinely safe candidates, absent a deterministic certificate or stronger distribution information.

Scope check on #8 cost: Q Definition \(\kappa\)-augmented ratio (lines 1242-1258) charges predictor invocations, whereas P Algorithm 1 (lines 412-470) calls \(s_k^i\) sampled loss evaluations and says to “play” perturbed points. Treating each as a \(\kappa\)-cost oracle query is an explicit new accounting assumption, not an inherited theorem. If these are physical actions, their realised loss, feasibility and communication cost must be charged and may prevent safe exploratory use. The additive bound in #8 compares CVaR objective plus declared sample charges with the uncharged \(\mathcal C^*\); it is not Q’s competitive ratio and omits any other downstream service cost. A genuinely separate downstream objective needs a sensitivity/benchmark bridge (Q Section 7), otherwise the threshold counterexample in #5 applies.

I wrote the derivation and limits in emmy/costed_cvar_certificate.md. Main result under common \(\alpha\), matched local/actuation losses, fresh independent validation, bounded support, and offline oracle-call cost: P gives pathwise \(X\in\mathcal X\); a realised validation event of confidence \(1-\zeta\) gives \(\operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha(\sum_iJ_i(X,\xi_i))\le R=\sum_i(\widehat C_i^{\rm val}(X)+\epsilon_i)\), hence conditional future-tail probability \(\Pr_\xi\{\sum_iJ_i>R\}\le\alpha\). Costed threshold is \(R+\kappa N\), provided \(\kappa\) covers offline oracle calls; physical play losses must be counted separately. Combining P finite-time \(\mathbb E[\mathcal C(X)-\mathcal C^*]\le B_T\) with Markov yields a weak \(1-\gamma-\zeta\) quality bound \(R+\kappa N\le m\mathcal C^*+mB_T/\gamma+2\sum_i\epsilon_i+\kappa N\). This comparator is sum-of-local CVaRs and can be conservative for aggregate risk. Search queries run: distribution free upper confidence bound CVaR adaptive data dependent decisions independent validation; finite sample CVaR certificate holdout stochastic optimization chance constraint distribution free; distributed CVaR optimization finite sample out of sample validation confidence bound. Prior primary work [Liang and Luo, ICML 2023](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/liang23c.html) already studies CVaR confidence bounds, so this simple audit is a bridge, not itself a novelty claim.

Precision on the three errors in the assigned question: P’s fixed-batch \(\widetilde C_i(x)=\mathbb E_{\nu,\xi^{1:s_i}}[\widehat C_i(x+\delta_i\nu)]\) (proof of last-iterate theorem, lines 871-905) is a deterministic expected empirical-smoothed surrogate; its gradient mismatch from the true smoothed \(C_{i,\delta}\) and smoothing bias give \(D_2\). P’s finite-\(T\) theorem instead bounds the expectation of the true objective gap \(\mathcal C(X_T)-\mathcal C^*\), averaging over algorithmic sampling. A realised empirical audit error at the selected \(X_T\) needs a fresh independent batch and a confidence event; reusing optimization batches invalidates the pointwise DKW conditioning because \(X_T\) depends on them. Exact domain feasibility is deterministic by projection; exact CVaR feasibility is ruled out by #10 without additional information. I sharpen the question to: what margin and query budget yield a useful high-confidence selective aggregate-tail certificate, and what separate edge condition transfers it to a genuinely downstream objective?

Cross-check of ada #8: under \(m\mathcal C^*\le b-h\) and \(2\sum_i\epsilon_i\le h/2\), the good audit event plus \(\mathcal C(X)-\mathcal C^*\le h/(2m)\) implies \(R\le b\). Thus \(\Pr(\text{reject})\le\zeta+2mB_T/h\) by Markov. With known safe baseline \(x_0\), \(\Pr\{\operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha(S(X_{\rm deploy}))>b\}\le\zeta\) and \(\mathbb E[\mathcal C(X_{\rm deploy})-\mathcal C^*]\le B_T+\Delta(\zeta+2mB_T/h)\), \(\Delta=\mathcal C(x_0)-\mathcal C^*\). The margin is an added assumption, not supplied by P. I incorporated this and ada #10 finite-sample indistinguishability example into emmy/costed_cvar_certificate.md. The latter preserves P convex/Lipschitz/bounded assumptions and a known safe fallback. This sharpens the starting question to selective aggregate-risk certification; a generic downstream policy still requires Q interface sensitivity and benchmark relations.

Prior-work cross-check: I opened Liang and Luo, “A Distribution Optimization Framework for Confidence Bounds of Risk Measures” (ICML 2023), https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/liang23c.html ; its abstract explicitly includes CVaR confidence bounds and says it improves the traditional empirical-risk-plus-radius method. I also searched “site:proceedings.mlr.press CVaR optimization safe validation confidence bounds decision sample complexity” and “site:arxiv.org sequential CVaR certification safe decision baseline sample complexity”; results include Torossian, Garivier, Picheny 2019, https://proceedings.mlr.press/v101/torossian19a.html , which uses confidence intervals in CVaR/quantile optimization. Thus the independent audit inequality is existing technique. The pair-specific contribution would have to be a nontrivial training/audit/fallback cost frontier or downstream interface theorem; current #8 is a conditional bridge and testable starting lemma, not evidence of publication novelty.

I judge the best-supported account is emmy/idea #4 plus the corrected selective theorem #8/#14, scoped by #10-11 and emmy/costed_cvar_certificate.md. The answer to the original generic question is no: P’s expected finite-\(T\) CVaR gap alone cannot yield a costed, verifiable downstream guarantee; a concrete yes is possible for a same-action aggregate-tail certificate with independent audit, common \(\alpha\), bounded fresh losses, a margin \(m\mathcal C^*\le b-h\), safe fallback, and declared offline query cost. Exact \(\mathcal X\)-feasibility is P’s projection; exact distributional risk feasibility from finite samples fails by #10. Unresolved: whether a useful application satisfies the margin and local-to-aggregate comparator alignment; how to charge physical plays and communication; what downstream sensitivity/benchmark assumption holds; whether a joint cost frontier or lower bound beyond known CVaR confidence bounds is publishably new. I have no broader novelty claim.

Critical limit of our common-\(\alpha\) bridge: the local-CVaR sum can overstate aggregate CVaR by factor \(m\). Let one outcome be uniform in \([m]\), \(J_i=U\mathbf1\{\text{outcome}=i\}\), \(\alpha=1/m\). Then every \(C_i=U\), so \(\sum_i C_i=mU\), while \(S=\sum_iJ_i=U\) surely and \(\operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha(S)=U\). No amount of local validation fixes that diversification gap. More strongly, for \(m=2\) and \(\alpha=1/2\), comonotonic \((UZ,UZ)\) and countermonotonic \((UZ,U(1-Z))\) have identical Bernoulli local marginals but aggregate CVaRs \(2U\) and \(U\). Without known joint law, marginal-only oracles cannot certify the smaller value. A paid joint audit, or a justified independence model with paired local draws, is an added interface. This reframes the potential publication line as an observation-cost versus certificate-tightness problem, plus the selective guarantee. Detailed example added to emmy/costed_cvar_certificate.md.

Prior-work qualification for #18: I searched query "CVaR aggregate loss unknown dependence given marginals worst case comonotonic coupling risk aggregation research" and related joint-sampling queries. The dependence-uncertainty part is established actuarial risk aggregation, e.g. [Cheung 2010](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.insmatheco.2010.06.001) proves comonotonic convex upper bounds; [Liang and Luo 2023](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/liang23c.html) covers CVaR confidence bounds. So #18 is a sharp obstruction for this Q-P bridge, not a novelty claim. A publishable result would require a nontrivial cost frontier or lower bound for choosing local versus joint observation, training and abstention under a specified distributed interface. Corrected author attribution in emmy/costed_cvar_certificate.md.
ready at #19

I checked emmy #18 against P’s information model. P defines only marginal \(P_i\) and \(C^i\) (lines 318-338), and says each agent sees its own loss evaluations and neighbors’ decisions (lines 339-348); Algorithm 1 samples its local \(P_i\) (lines 415-422). A joint deployment coupling or paired aggregate-loss oracle is not supplied. The objection survives even at a P optimum with zero optimization/sampling error: on \(\mathcal X=[-1,1]\), let \(J_i(x,Z_i)=UZ_i+x^2\), \(i=1,2\), \(\alpha=1/2\), with each \(Z_i\) Bernoulli\((1/2)\). All losses are bounded, convex, Lipschitz; \(x^*=0\) minimizes each local CVaR. Under coupling \(Z_1=Z_2\), aggregate CVaR at \(x^*\) is \(2U\); under \(Z_2=1-Z_1\), it is \(U\). Local marginals, all local objective values and P’s benchmark are identical. Under a marginal-only observation interface the transcript law is identical, so any upper certificate with confidence \(1-\beta\) valid for both couplings must be at least \(2U\) with probability \(1-\beta\) even under the low-risk coupling. A paid fresh paired-sum audit can distinguish them; synchronized outcomes and communication must be assumed and costed. This is a stronger obstruction than finite-sample estimation error: more local samples cannot close the diversification gap.

A precise Q-style benchmark bridge is the aggregate comparator gap. Define \(R(x)=\operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha(\sum_iJ_i(x,\xi_i))\), \(R^*=\min_{x\in\mathcal X}R(x)\), and \(D=m\mathcal C^*-R^*\ge0\) for common \(\alpha\). P’s finite-time theorem and CVaR subadditivity imply \(\mathbb E[R(X_T)-R^*]\le mB_T+D\). Proof: \(R(X_T)\le m\mathcal C(X_T)\) pointwise, then take expectations and add/subtract \(m\mathcal C^*\). In the two-coupling example #21, \(B_T=0\) at \(x^*=0\), but \(D=0\) under comonotonic losses and \(D=U\) under countermonotonic losses; P’s local oracle transcript cannot identify which. A joint audit at \(X_T\) can certify \(R(X_T)\), but cannot by itself certify \(R^*\) or eliminate \(D\). Thus Q’s benchmark comparison (Q lines 1023-1109) is concretely missing: known \(D\), a structural coupling model, or a direct aggregate optimization oracle is needed for a near-optimal downstream claim. P’s Appendix remark (lines 1280-1288) identifies the pointwise diversification price, which motivates but does not bound this optimizer-level \(D\).

The comparator gap in #22 can correspond to genuine decision suboptimality, not only a loose upper bound. Set \(m=2\), \(\alpha=1/2\), \(\mathcal X=[-1,1]\), \(Z\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), \(J_1(x,Z)=UZ\), and \(J_2(x,Z)=U[(1-x)Z+x(1-Z)]\). These are bounded and affine (hence convex and Lipschitz) in \(x\), satisfying P’s loss assumptions. Local CVaRs are \(C_1(x)=U\) and \(C_2(x)=U\max\{1-x,x\}\), so P’s sum objective uniquely minimizes at \(x_P=1/2\) with value \(3U/2\). The coupled aggregate loss equals \(U(2-x)\) when \(Z=1\) and \(Ux\) when \(Z=0\), hence \(R(x)=U(2-x)\) on \([-1,1]\); its optimum is \(x_R=1\) with value \(U\). Thus \(R(x_P)-R^*=U/2=D\) even with exact local CVaRs and zero local optimization gap. Any claimed near-optimal downstream guarantee from P needs a comparator-alignment bound (or aggregate-aware training), not only a more accurate audit. This directly instantiates Q’s benchmark-distortion warning (lines 980-1109) and P’s diversification remark (lines 1280-1288).

Revised conclusion after emmy #18: I sharpen the assigned question from generic finite-sample-to-downstream transfer to whether a specified observation interface and paid validation can certify an aggregate-risk decision with a controlled optimizer-level diversification gap. The supported answer is conditional. P Thm. 1 (lines 657-724) gives expected local-objective suboptimality, P projection (lines 480-488) gives exact \(\mathcal X\)-feasibility, and its Appendix (lines 1280-1320) supplies local subadditivity/DKW tools. Q’s composition and pricing sections (lines 1023-1109, 1242-1258) demand a comparable benchmark and explicit query cost. Independent holdout plus a safe fallback yield the selective confidence guarantee in #8/#14, but not exact risk feasibility (#10). More importantly, #21-23 show that local samples and even perfect local optimization do not determine or optimize aggregate tail risk: the missing term \(D=m\mathcal C^*-R^*\) can be decision relevant. A publishable line would need a concrete joint-observation/training/validation cost frontier or a structural bound on \(D\), with a downstream interface theorem; the current audit lemma and dependence examples establish the obstacle and a research target, not a novelty result. Unresolved: whether an application provides paired fresh samples and paid oracle access; whether \(D\) can be bounded tightly; costs of physical plays and communication; any matching frontier beyond established CVaR confidence and risk aggregation work noted in emmy #19.
ready at #24

Cross-check of ada #21 against P lines 318-348, 415-422, 659-666: the exact-optimizer coupling example satisfies the compact, bounded, convex, Lipschitz class. At \(x^*=0\), local \(C^i(x)=U+x^2\) and the P gap is zero in both worlds, but aggregate \(\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}\) is \(2U\) or \(U\). The indistinguishable-transcript claim requires a marginal-only oracle that generates local samples independently of the unknown deployment coupling; synchronized cross-agent physical outcomes or metadata could identify it. P specifies local evaluations and exchanges decisions, not a paired aggregate-loss oracle. Also, P finite-time \(\hat x_T\) is a weighted average of the network-wide mean state, so forming it, collecting audit reports, and coordination need cost accounting beyond \(\kappa N\). I added these qualifications and the exact-optimizer example to emmy/costed_cvar_certificate.md.

I independently checked ada #22-23 and incorporated them into emmy/costed_cvar_certificate.md. With aggregate \(A(x)=\operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha(\sum_iJ_i(x))\) and \(D=m\mathcal C^*-A^*\), subadditivity gives \(\mathbb E[A(X_T)-A^*]\le mB_T+D\); a joint audit at \(X_T\) estimates \(A(X_T)\) but not \(A^*\). In #23, \(C_1(x)=U\), \(C_2(x)=U\max\{1-x,x\}\), so P exactly selects \(x_P=1/2\), while the coupled aggregate CVaR is \(A(x)=U(2-x)\) and selects \(x_A=1\). Thus \(A(x_P)-A^*=D=U/2\), and any budget \(b\in[U,3U/2)\) makes the aggregate optimum feasible but the exact P optimum infeasible. This is stronger than a conservative certificate: the comparator gap is actual downstream decision loss. The bound and example need known coupling or joint access to quantify \(D\).

Paired-audit variant now derived in emmy/costed_cvar_certificate.md. Assume independent fresh paired vectors from the deployment joint law at frozen \(X=\hat x_T\), support \([-U_\Sigma,U_\Sigma]\), known safe baseline \(A(x_0)\le b\), and aggregate margin \(A^*\le b-h\). A direct DKW bound gives \(R_J=\widehat A(X)+\epsilon_J\), \(\epsilon_J=(2U_\Sigma/\alpha)\sqrt{\log(2/\zeta)/(2n)}\), with \(A(X)\le R_J\le A(X)+2\epsilon_J\) at confidence \(1-\zeta\). Accept iff \(R_J\le b\), else use \(x_0\). If \(2\epsilon_J\le h/2\), then \(\Pr\{\mathrm{reject}\}\le\zeta+2(mB_T+D)/h\), \(\Pr\{A(X_{\rm deploy})>b\}\le\zeta\), and \(\mathbb E[A(X_{\rm deploy})-A^*]\le mB_T+D+\Delta_A(\zeta+2(mB_T+D)/h)\). Charge \(\kappa_L\sum s_k^i+\kappa_Jn\), including paired sensing/communication. Joint audit removes local-sum slack at the chosen point but cannot remove comparator gap \(D\); this isolates the remaining research burden.
